Uzbektelecom JSC Enters Insolvency, Raising Questions Over National Telecom Services

Tashkent—Uzbekistan’s largest fixed-line and internet provider, Uzbektelecom JSC, has entered insolvency proceedings, the company confirmed on Thursday, sending shockwaves through the country’s telecommunications sector and raising concerns over the continuity of essential services.

The state-owned operator, which serves millions of subscribers across all 14 regions, cited “unmanageable debts and sustained financial difficulties” as the main drivers behind its decision. Court-appointed administrators are now overseeing day-to-day operations, while a full financial assessment is underway.

“We are committed to maintaining network stability and service for all customers during this challenging period,” said Murodjon Sattarov, head of administration at Uzbektelecom JSC. “Our teams are working closely with regulators and stakeholders to ensure telephone and internet connectivity remain uninterrupted.”

However, customers in several areas reported intermittent disruptions to internet access and delays in customer service on Thursday. “We’ve seen slower speeds and longer downtimes in the last few days,” said Gulbahor Rakhimova, a small business owner in Samarkand. “It’s worrying for businesses like mine that depend on stable internet.”

Analysts warn that continued uncertainty could have ripple effects across Uzbekistan’s digital economy. “Uzbektelecom’s position as an infrastructure backbone means its troubles could hamper digital services, fintech, and even government operations,” said Timur Yuldashev, telecom sector analyst at Global Insights Group. According to Yuldashev, the company holds around 70% of the nation’s fixed-line and broadband market.

The Uzbekistan Telecommunications Workers Union expressed concern for the company’s 14,000 employees, many of whom face an anxious wait over potential layoffs or delayed salaries. “Our members are dedicated to keeping the network running, but we urgently need clarity over their future,” said union representative Dilshod Akhmedov.

The Ministry of Digital Technologies said in a statement it is “monitoring the situation closely” and is prepared to intervene if service continuity is threatened. Industry sources suggest that a restructuring, asset sale, or even partial privatization may be considered by administrators, although no decisions have yet been made public.

As insolvency proceedings continue, businesses and households nationwide are bracing for further updates, with many hoping for swift resolution to secure one of Uzbekistan’s most critical networks.
